title: [feat] Bootstrap Vite + TypeScript + Netlify Functions project layout
body:
## What

Scaffold the Vite + TS + Netlify Functions project so subsequent issues have a place to land.

## Why

Every other issue assumes the project layout exists. Without this, no work can begin.

## How

- `package.json` with `dev`, `build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test` scripts
- `tsconfig.json` strict mode, target ES2022, bundler resolution
- `vite.config.ts` (Vite, vanilla-ts preset)
- `netlify.toml` with the WebMCP-required headers
- `public/index.html` shell with the Lattice title
- `netlify/functions/` empty placeholder
- ESLint + Prettier config

## Acceptance

- [ ] `netlify dev` serves the index page on http://localhost:8888
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] `curl -I http://localhost:8888` returns the WebMCP headers
- [ ] Site is deployable to Netlify

title: [chore] Add netlify.toml headers required by the WebMCP spec
body:
## What

Every Netlify response must include the headers the WebMCP spec requires for tool registration to succeed.

## How

In `netlify.toml`:

```toml
[[headers]]
  for = "/*"
  [headers.values]
    Origin-Agent-Cluster = "?1"
    Permissions-Policy = "tools=(self)"
```

## Why

Without these, `registerTool` rejects with `NotAllowedError`. A judge who runs the demo will see this and dock the score.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `curl -I http://localhost:8888/` shows both headers
- [ ] The dev server is verified to register a test tool successfully

- [ ] It is referenced from README and CONTRIBUTING

title: [research] Decide: should we expose MCP resources alongside tools?
body:
## What

The MCP spec has three primitives: tools, prompts, resources. WebMCP demos almost exclusively use tools. Resources are a different model: server-pushed, addressable by URI, the agent reads them.

## Question

Should Lattice expose `lattice://papers/{id}/page/{n}` as a resource? It would let the agent "read" a paper page the way it reads a tool result, with a different trust boundary.

## Why it matters

Resources are underused in WebMCP. If we use them well, the demo reads differently to a judge. If we use them poorly, it's complexity for no gain.

## Deliverable

A 200-word recommendation: do we ship resources? If yes, which ones, and what do they enable? If no, why not?

title: [research] Decide: do we adopt the in-PR icons annotation on tools?
body:
## What

## Question

## Deliverable

title: [feat] Implement two-column read-order reconstruction
body:
## What

The headline problem for academic PDFs. Two-column papers interleave left-column-bottom with right-column-top in pdf.js's textContent output. Fix it.

## Approach

1. Detect column count per page (look for a horizontal gap in the y-distribution of glyphs)
2. If single column: sort by y descending, then x ascending
3. If two columns: split glyphs at the column boundary, sort within each column by y descending, then concatenate left-column then right-column
4. Recombine paragraphs by detecting line breaks (y jumps > 1.5 line height)

## Acceptance

- [ ] A 5-paper test set has correct read order (verified by a human)
- [ ] Single-column papers are not regressed
- [ ] Equations and tables are skipped
